welcome.title: How do phone calls feel to you?
welcome.p1: Welcome. You are about to take part in the first study of the Institute for The Study Of Humanity: Study 7, Stage A.
welcome.p2: It measures how common phone anxiety and other phone-related difficulties are, both overall and in different groups, including people with and without ADHD or autism. We need answers from everyone, including people who find phone calls easy. First results will be published in October.
welcome.p3: It takes about three minutes. It is anonymous: no name, email or account. The page notes how long each question takes and how far you get, even if you stop; your answers are sent only when you press Send.
welcome.p4: Next, choose a focus sound and a time signal if you want them, then tap Continue. After that, set your timer: pick a short or long call, or set your own duration with the picker.
welcome.repeat_note: This device has sent answers before. You are welcome to continue; please answer the last question honestly.

under18.title: Thank you for wanting to take part.
under18.p1: This questionnaire is for adults, so it ends here. Nothing about you was recorded, only that someone under 18 visited.
under18.p2: A version for people under 18 is planned. Maximized Impact ry announces the Institute's studies and results on Instagram, so following is the way to hear when it opens.

survey.title: How do phone calls feel to you?
survey.intro1: Anonymous, about three minutes. No names, no email, no account. Run by the Institute for The Study Of Humanity, a research initiative of Maximized Impact ry.
survey.intro2: As you answer, the page records how long each question takes and how far you get, even if you stop before the end. Your answers themselves are only sent when you press Send answers.
survey.credit: Timer and focus tools adapted from Yapper Phone.

c3.text: In the past year I have avoided something important (an appointment, a bill, a job, a health matter) because it required a phone call.

d2.text: I find it hard to end a call even when I want to.

file.title: Your answers
file.study_line: Study 7: telephone anxiety and call avoidance
file.no_identifiers: This file contains no name, email, device or account identifier. Nothing in it links to you.
file.thank_you_p1: You have just helped put a number on how phone calls feel, for people with and without ADHD or autism. As far as we know, no one has measured this before. Every answer in this file is part of that number.
file.thank_you_p2: The Institute for The Study Of Humanity received your answers anonymously. This copy is yours: keep it, share it, or delete it. The Institute cannot connect it to you, and it holds nothing that could.
file.question: Question
file.tools_p: The survey page offered the same call-length timer, focus sounds and time signals that Yapper Phone uses inside a call. What you chose is recorded here for you and, without any identifier, alongside your answers, so the Institute can see which tools people prefer.
file.next_p1: The results are published open access under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, with a summary in Finnish and English, as an addendum to the white paper "The Case for Health Communications Technology" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21978705). You will find them at research.maximized-impact.org/study7/results. The anonymised dataset is published with the results so that anyone can check the numbers.
file.next_p2: If you have a question about the study, write to janne@maximized-impact.org. Because the Institute holds no identifiers, it cannot find or remove an individual submission after it has been sent; this file is your record.
file.footer: Institute for The Study Of Humanity · Maximized Impact ry · Helsinki, Finland

data_notice.title: What this page collects
data_notice.p1: When you press Send, your answers are sent to the Institute for The Study Of Humanity with no name, email, account, phone number or device identifier. The Institute does not store IP addresses. A random session code links the parts of one visit together and nothing else.
data_notice.p2: While you answer, the page sends two small progress signals, when you start and if you leave, so the Institute can see where people stop. They contain no answers.
data_notice.p3: Your browser keeps one flag saying this device has answered, so the page can remind you. The page sets no cookies and uses no analytics. When you press Send, an invisible bot check by Cloudflare Turnstile confirms that a person is sending the answers; it is the only third-party service on the page.
data_notice.p4: Results are published open access with the anonymised dataset. Because no identifier exists, a submission cannot be found or removed afterwards.
